sentences.text:
Petitioners are before this Court seeking anticipatory bail apprehending arrest on the complaint of Smt. Dharshini J.R. wife of the first petitioner herein, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter referred to as 'IPC'
for short) and under Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (hereinafter referred to as 'DP Act' for short).
2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
3.
The marriage of petitioner No.1 with Smt. Dharshini J.R. was solemnized on 07.02.2022 at Krishna Kalyana Mantapa, 2nd Main Road, Industrial Town, Rajajinagar, Bangalore - 560 044.

It appears that relationship between the couple got strained due to some difference of opinion and as a result, Smt. Dharshini J.R. had approached Karnataka State Women's Commission (hereinafter referred to as 'the Commission' for short) and had filed a complaint on 06.04.2023 NC:
2023:KHC:29092 regarding harassment and demand for dowry against the petitioners.

4. It is the case of the petitioners that they have been threatened before the Commission in the event they do not settle the matter with the complainant, a criminal case will be registered against them and they would be put behind bar and it is under these circumstances, they had filed Crl.Misc.
No.2640/2023 before the Court of LXXI Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru City (CCH-72), which came to be dismissed on 25.03.2023.

entities.text: Court of LXXI Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru City
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Under these circumstances, the petitioners are before this Court.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner reiterating the grounds urged in the bail petition submits that there is a genuine threat of arrest and therefore, the petitioners are before this Court.
6.

Per contra, the learned HCGP on instructions submits that there is no complaint lodged by Smt.
Dharshini J.R. against the petitioners for the alleged offences and the apprehension of the petitioners is ill-founded.

She also submits that there is no threat from the Commission regarding arrest of NC: 2023:KHC:29092 the petitioners and therefore, the petitioners are not entitled for the relief of anticipatory bail.

7. Considering the nature of the allegations made in the complaint and also having regard to the fact that from 06.04.2023 onwards till date, the complainant has not approached the police, it appears that the apprehension of the petitioners is ill-founded.

8. Learned HCGP on instruction has also made a submission that no FIR has been registered against the petitioners for the aforesaid offences and also submits that for an offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC, without following the guidelines issued by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, accused will not be arrested.
9.
Under these circumstances, I am of the view that petitioner's apprehension is ill-founded, and therefore, they are not entitled for the relief sought for in the petition.
Accordingly, the petition is disposed off.
